name: WISE 0855−0714
tagline: Coldest brown dwarf, hidden by a neighbour
blurb: The coldest known brown dwarf (about −20 °C). Too faint for one SPHEREx exposure; only a stack of the longest-wavelength exposures can show it.
notes: In 2025–26 it passes 4–11″ from a Gaia G = 16.3 background star, inside SPHEREx's aperture: the light measured here is mostly that star, so this is not a detection of WISE 0855.

target.source: AllWISE J085510.74-071442.5 position; motion Luhman & Esplin 2016 (UNVERIFIED in PLAN.md)

cube.note: SPHEREx all-sky spectral map: each channel is the average of every visit up to the release, so different channels at one spot come from different dates.

finecube.note: Built from the single SPHEREx exposures at 6.15" pixels: each channel averages every exposure whose wavelength at that spot falls in it, over all visits, so different channels come from different dates.

flags.meaning: percent of the visit's exposures on that detector flagged at the pixel (255 = not covered)

colour_hint: WISE 0855 is lost in the light of a brighter background star 4–11″ away, so there is nothing special to see in colour here: one 12.9″ pixel can't tell two objects that close apart.

provenance.label: IRSA DR1+QR3 (baked 2026-11-15)
provenance.credit: Data: NASA/JPL-Caltech/IPAC (IRSA). Not a NASA product.
